\begin{abstract}
Schema Mutation (benchmark-schema-mutation) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.1.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0 over 60 tasks, from mock runs at seeds 1 and 2; it declares no public task-split seed. The review record shows 2 fix rounds, 2 defect classes with public locators, and 12 merged feature pull requests of which 11 were approved. It was not part of the preregistered trivial-policy check. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422412, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}
\section{What the package asks}
The package states its question in its own README:
% quote: benchmark-schema-mutation/README.md#L7
\begin{quote}
APIs change under a model's feet. A field gets renamed, an enum gains
new values, one endpoint splits into two \textemdash{} and the model
has to decide between the schema in front of it and the one it
memorized in training. benchmark-schema-mutation measures that choice:
60 tasks, each one a freshly migrated tool schema plus a user request,
graded by exact match on the emitted JSON tool call.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-schema-mutation/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#L7}{\texttt{benchmark-schema-mutation:README.md\#L7}}.}

Its index entry states the measured construct as: ``Whether a model follows the current tool schema after a migration, renamed fields, new required fields, changed enums, split endpoints and type changes, instead of the version it memorized.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-schema-mutation.whatItMeasures}).

\section{Grader and surfaces}
The grading document states the mechanism in its own words:
% quote: benchmark-schema-mutation/docs/grading.md#L5
\begin{quote}
Each task asks for one JSON tool call: \texttt{\{"name": "<tool>",
"arguments": \{...\}\}}. The grader extracts that object from the raw
answer, unwraps common wire formats, normalises it, canonicalises it
(object keys sorted recursively; arrays keep order), and compares the
result to the \texttt{expected} string stored on the task after the
same normalisation. A canonical match against \texttt{metadata.stale}
(the call that was correct under the pre-migration schema) scores 0
and is flagged \texttt{staleSchemaUsed} in the reason and details.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-schema-mutation/blob/v0.1.0/docs/grading.md#L5}{\texttt{benchmark-schema-mutation:docs/grading.md\#L5}}.}

The index entry summarises the grader as: ``Canonical JSON equality on the tool name and arguments after normalisation; exact matches against the pre-migration call are reported as staleSchemaUsed.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-schema-mutation.grader}).

\section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records mock runs at seeds \pkgMockSeedA{} and \pkgMockSeedB{}
on version \pkgVersion{}. The package declares no public task-split seed. The recorded numbers:
the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}),
the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}),
and the run at mock seed \pkgMockSeedA{} scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks
with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}).
Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.
The README prints a sample run:

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set
at \pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{} through a local fake model server answering through
the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
This package was not part of the preregistered check, so \texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv} carries no row for it.
\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-schema-mutation/README.md#L122
\begin{quote}
The mutation catalogue is authored, so the 60 tasks cover five kinds
well but not every real-world migration (deprecation warnings,
paginated renames, OAuth scope shifts).
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-schema-mutation/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#L122}{\texttt{benchmark-schema-mutation:README.md\#L122}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models.
These offline numbers describe the graders and the scripted policies. They say nothing about a hosted model.
Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}).
Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here
are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
